## The well-balanced face positivity fallback {#sec-ch08-wbface}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md 8.9
status: draft
-->

### Summary

The well-balanced path reconstructs a perturbation about a hydrostatic reference and adds the reference
back at the face. Near the top of a column the reference is tiny and a nonlinear overshoot in the
perturbation can take the sum below zero. This fallback catches that, and the choice of what to fall
back to is the interesting part.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Keep the well-balanced $x_1$ face states positive after the reference is added back.

**Data.** In: the reconstructed perturbations, the reference pressure and density at the faces, the cell density. Out: face states patched in place.

**Placement.** In `HydroImpl::forward`, right after the $x_1$ reconstruction of the well-balanced path.

**Activation.** With gravity along $x_1$, a pressure row and a non-shallow-water equation of state; the ordinary face floors are off there.

**Guarantee / limits.** A no-op at rest, so well-balancing survives; the density fallback is a neighbour's value, not the reconstruction's.

**Evidence.** `[C6]` of `floors_check`; the well-balanced tests of @sec-ch05 indirectly.
:::

### Derivation

The pressure case is the simple one: a face pressure that comes out non-positive is replaced by the reference pressure
at that face, at `psf_lo` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). The reference is positive by
construction, and at rest the perturbation is zero, so the condition is never met and the well-balanced property
survives untouched. `[C6]` checks both halves of that. At rest the face pressure is the reference bit for bit at all
$2\times10^5$ faces and never non-positive, so the fallback cannot fire. Once a perturbation is allowed the fallback
fires at $23\,949$ of them and the result is strictly positive at every face [check
`src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch08/checks/floors_check.out`].

The density case is where a reasonable-looking choice is wrong, and the code comment at `dsf`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) records why from experience rather than from theory.
Falling back to the reference density fails when the reference overestimates the density aloft. A bottom-anchored
isentrope did so by orders of magnitude, and every floor event at a reflecting top wall then became a large spurious
wall impedance. The fallback is therefore the adjacent cell's density, which is a real local value rather than an
extrapolated reference.

A second detail in the same block is a latent-bug note worth carrying into the report. The shift along $x_1$ uses edge
replication rather than a circular roll. The comment at `density`[^rg-bdccc583b763]
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) says plainly that the circular word is not consumed
today, but would become live the moment a caller changed the face range. That is a hazard recorded in the code and not
a current defect.

### Numerical method

The block is `copy_` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). The reconstruction that feeds it
is called with floors switched off at `wtmp` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), precisely
because the ordinary reconstruction floors would clamp a legitimate negative perturbation. This fallback replaces them
for this path.

**Why these fallbacks.** Three facts of the code.

1. A non-positive face pressure is replaced by the reference pressure at that face, which is positive by construction
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
2. A non-positive face density is replaced by the adjacent cell's density, not the reference. A reference that
   overestimates the density aloft turned every floor event at a reflecting top wall into a spurious impedance, as the
   code comment records from a run.
3. At rest the perturbation is zero, so neither condition is met and the balanced state is untouched. `[C6]` finds the
   face pressure equal to the reference bit for bit at all $2\times10^5$ faces.

: Code map of the well-balanced face fallback. {#tbl-ch08-wbface-code}

**How to use it.** There is no switch of its own. The block runs when `wb_x1` is true, that is with gravity along
$x_1$, a pressure row and an equation of state other than `shallow-water`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). The pressure fallback is these lines:

```cpp
      auto pl = wtmp[ILT][IPR] + psf_lo;
      auto pr = wtmp[IRT][IPR] + psf_lo;
      wtmp[ILT][IPR].copy_(torch::where(pl > 0., pl, psf_lo));
      wtmp[IRT][IPR].copy_(torch::where(pr > 0., pr, psf_lo));
```

and the density fallback these:

```cpp
      wtmp[ILT][IDN].copy_(torch::where(dl > 0., dl, rho_below));
      wtmp[IRT][IDN].copy_(torch::where(dr > 0., dr, density));
```

`psf_lo` is the reference pressure at the lower face, `dl` and `dr` the reconstructed face densities with the
reference added. `density` is the cell density and `rho_below` the same shifted one cell down with edge replication.

The chapter's check ports the pressure fallback on a synthetic column.[^ch08-wbface-run] `[C6]`: at rest the face
pressure equals the reference bit for bit at $200\,000$ of $200\,000$ faces and is never non-positive. With a
perturbation the fallback fires at $23\,949$ faces and the result is strictly positive at every face. The density
fallback is not checked: **missing evidence**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The density fallback substitutes a neighbouring cell's density into a face state. That is a local
  value, but it is not the reconstruction's answer, and nothing measures the error it introduces when
  it fires.
:::

1. **Hypothesis, from a run not reproduced here.** That the reference-density fallback caused a large
   spurious wall impedance is recorded in the code comment from a bottom-anchored isentrope case. This
   chapter cites that reasoning; it does not reproduce the run.
2. **A latent hazard.** The edge-replication note describes a wraparound that is unreachable with
   today's face range. It is recorded because the range is the only thing keeping it unreachable.
